why: State cycle 2 (docs/v3/cycles/state-2.md, P2 state-2.1): cycle 1's fix (state-1.20) gave `createBasaltRouter` a `live` option, but `bindInvalidation(client, channel, o)` needs the client, and `createBasaltRouter` builds it inside (`provider/create-router.tsx:114`) and refuses one from the app, so `live` cannot be written the way `docs/bind-invalidation.md` shows it. The v3 path the shipped rule prescribes (`routerDefaults` and the `main.tpl` scaffold, 'never `createBasaltRouter`') has no `live` at all, nor does the v3 `BasaltProvider` in `basalt-ui/core/provider`. The cycle page starts the binding in its own effect from `useQueryClient()`.
what: An app starts its push binding through the kit on the path it actually uses.
owns: packages/basalt-ui/src/provider/create-router.tsx (`live` also as a function of the client)
packages/basalt-ui/agent/templates/main.tpl (a commented `live` line, if the template budget allows)
their tests; the export-surface snapshot through its generator
change: (1) The v3 `BasaltProvider` (`basalt-ui/core/provider`) takes `live?: { start(): () => void }` and starts it once on the client when it mounts, stopping it on unmount, never on the server, as `createBasaltRouter`'s option does. (2) `createBasaltRouter`'s and `basaltRouterOptions`' `live` also takes `(client: QueryClient) => { start(): () => void }`, called with the client they build. (3) `docs/bind-invalidation.md` shows the v3 wiring first: the module-level client of `main.tpl`, `bindInvalidation(queryClient, channel, o)`, then `<BasaltProvider live={live}>`.
commits: feat: one commit per surface in packages/basalt-ui; a contract amendment commit first if the provider props are frozen.
proof: make check; a provider test that counts start and stop across mount, rerender and unmount; a router test of the function form.
acceptance: The v3 BasaltProvider starts a `live` binding once on mount and stops it on unmount; a server render starts nothing (test)
createBasaltRouter accepts `live: (client) => binding` and starts it with the client it built (test)
docs/bind-invalidation.md shows a wiring that compiles on the routerDefaults path
out_of_scope: Removing the cycle build's effect (the next cycle does); the 2.x provider beyond the function form.
